title: Translate a Claude Code session in the home into a Codex 0.156.0 rollout with a loss account beside it
purpose: Translation to another harness is designed and not proved. This brief proves the first one, for one named pair, Claude Code to Codex 0.156.0, and nothing above it assumes it. A lys-home subcommand renders a home session that was imported from Claude Code as a Codex rollout in the shape Codex 0.156.0 writes for its own threads, measured from files that version wrote and never assumed from a source checkout. Every text part, tool call and tool result is carried whole, readable thinking is carried as text and opaque blocks are dropped by hash (home P3), the rollout announces itself in band as a translated context, and a JSON loss account beside it lists by entry id and block hash what was kept, what changed shape and how, and what was lost and why. It improves on Codex's own importer of Claude Code files, which is a compaction and not a copy, and neither adopts nor calls it (ADR-014, ADR-004). Each translation is recorded on the home session as a side leaf the way a template render is (ADR-012), and the proof is a real resume by Codex 0.156.0 in an isolated Codex home.
task: Start by recording and measuring (R1): nothing about the rollout's shape is taken from a Codex source checkout or from a rollout another Codex version wrote. The machine that builds this brief has two Codex binaries, and the one that comes first on PATH is an older version, so every Codex run in this brief names the binary that answers `--version` with `codex-cli 0.156.0` by its absolute path, and the proof names which binary it ran. Every Codex run in this brief uses an isolated Codex home made under a temporary directory (CODEX_HOME), with its own sessions tree and thread index, never the user's own Codex home; the proof calls it <codex home>. The subcommand is `lys-home render-codex --home <home> --session <id> --out <target directory> --codex-version <version>`. It takes exactly those four arguments. It does not take a canon: the Claude Code render's optional canon is not placed before a Codex translation. The only version it renders for is 0.156.0; any other version, 0.156.1 included, is refused naming the version asked for and the version the shape was measured on, and a later card adds a version when it is measured. It walks Session::context_path(), the same path the Claude Code render walks: that path already begins at the last compaction boundary and carries that boundary's summary. A Claude Code session's meta records were imported as ordinary messages, so their text parts are carried whole like every other text part (Codex's importer drops them; this render does not). Sidechains hang off the context path under a label naming the agent, so they are not rendered and the loss account names each sidechain entry as lost. Harness events, labels and every lys custom entry (lys.harness_event, lys.call, lys.authored, lys.inherited, lys.given, and any later lys type such as a lantern) are not rendered and are named as lost. A Claude tool call becomes Codex's function_call item and its result Codex's function_call_output item, paired by call_id; the Claude tool_use id is carried as the call_id, the tool name is carried whole, and the input object is carried as the arguments string, the compact JSON serialisation of the stored input value (serde_json::to_string), whatever JSON value it is. The function pair is chosen over custom_tool_call because a Claude tool input is a JSON value, which a function_call's JSON arguments string carries whole and reversibly, while a custom tool's input is free text for a grammar. A block hash in the loss account is the key of the block HOME-001's importer stored: the SHA-256 of serde_json::to_vec of the Claude-shaped source part, which is recovered from the Pi part by the inverse of the importer's mapping (text to text; thinking to thinking with signature; redacted thinking to redacted_thinking with data; toolCall to tool_use with input; a toolResult message to its tool_result part, trying the content as a single string and as the stored array, with and without is_error) and taken as the first candidate the home's block store holds. The loss account never names the SHA-256 of a re-serialised Pi part, since nobody can find that hash in blocks/. Thread ids, item ids, turn ids and timestamps are derived from the source, never random and never the clock, so the same session at the same head renders the same bytes: the thread id is the uuid shaped (as render::record_uuid shapes one) from the SHA-256 of the source session id, a colon and the source head hash; an item's ids come from the SHA-256 of its source entry id and part index; each line's timestamp is its source entry's timestamp, and the file-name timestamp is the head entry's. The model and model provider written into the lines that carry them are the values the recorded fixture carries, held as constants beside the version. The rollout's lines, their order and each item's fields are the ones R1 measures: every field the recorded fixture's item of that kind carries and no other. The acceptance for the fixture match compares response_item payloads only, since other line kinds carry the thread's runtime; it ignores the fields named id, call_id and turn_id, the create_time inside the passthrough metadata, and each line's timestamp, and compares a function_call's arguments as parsed JSON, since the fixture's Claude input is an object. call_id pairing is checked separately. Codex's importer clipped tool input at 2,000 characters and tool results at 4,000 as read from a source checkout, not from 0.156.0; the test carries a 16,384-character tool result and an 8,192-character tool input, well above both, and checks each by length and SHA-256. In scope: the codex harness module, the subcommand, the translation side leaf, both fixtures, the tests, RECORD.md, the crate README and PROOF-TRANSLATE.md. The cluster design's non-goal on other harnesses was narrowed to Claude Code and Codex 0.156.0 with this brief; HOME-001's own boundary is unchanged, since it bounded HOME-001. Out of scope: Codex to Claude Code, which exists in no tree here; adopting, vendoring, linking or calling Codex's importer, or copying any Codex code; Pi or any third harness; launching Codex through a launch template, which is that template's next version; writing any Codex thread index or any file under the user's own Codex home; image parts, whose carriage is not settled (see R4).

requirements.title: Record a Codex 0.156.0 rollout as the fixture and measure its shape and how Codex finds it
requirements.spec: Before any render code is written, record the fixture rollout from Codex 0.156.0 itself. In a fresh isolated Codex home, run the binary that answers `--version` with `codex-cli 0.156.0`, by its absolute path, on a synthetic prompt that holds no transcript and no personal content, in a thread in which Codex makes at least one call it records as a function_call item and records its function_call_output item, and answers with text. Keep that rollout file whole as the fixture. Then write in the codex module's docs, measured from that file and from Codex resuming copies of it: the directory and file-name pattern 0.156.0 writes a rollout under; the line kinds it writes and their order; the fields of session_meta, turn_context and of each response_item kind in the fixture (message, function_call, function_call_output, and reasoning when present); whether a compaction item written by 0.156.0 carries readable summary text, measured from rollouts 0.156.0 wrote, and the item kind the render uses for a compaction as a result; the role and item kind the in-band marker takes, measured from rollouts Codex's importer wrote carrying its <EXTERNAL SESSION IMPORTED> marker; and whether `codex resume <thread id>` in a fresh isolated Codex home finds a rollout copied under its sessions tree with no thread index written by hand, and which line kinds that resume needs, found by resuming copies with one non-response_item line kind removed at a time. The module SHALL hold the measured version (0.156.0) and the model and model provider the fixture carries as constants. THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT take any shape from a Codex source checkout or from a rollout another Codex version wrote, SHALL NOT write under the user's own Codex home, SHALL NOT write any Codex thread index by hand, and SHALL NOT put any transcript content in the fixture. IF the fixture holds a response_item that no Claude Code record could be the source of (a developer message, an environment-context message, a reasoning item), THEN the scout SHALL name the item kinds, and the fixture match in R7 waits on the lead's answer to the open question on them.
acceptance: tests/fixtures/codex/rollout-0.156.0.jsonl exists, every line parses as JSON, its session_meta payload's cli_version is "0.156.0", and it holds at least one response_item of type function_call and one of type function_call_output with equal call_id.
harness/codex/mod.rs holds the constant CODEX_VERSION equal to "0.156.0", and constants for the model and model provider whose values equal the fixture's.

harness/codex/mod.rs's module docs name the rollout directory and file-name pattern, the line kinds in order, the fields of each response_item kind in the fixture, the item kind used for a compaction, the marker's role and item kind, and the outcome of the resume of a copied rollout in a fresh isolated Codex home.
harness/codex/mod.rs contains no `fn` item.

requirements.title: Name the Codex render's refusals
requirements.spec: Add to HomeError: UnmeasuredCodexVersion, carrying the version asked for and the version the shape was measured on; UncarriedPart, carrying the entry id and the part kind of a part this brief does not carry; and BlockNotStored, carrying the entry id and the part index of a part none of whose source reconstructions the block store holds. Each message SHALL name those values and SHALL NOT carry any byte of a part's content. An existing target path is refused with the existing HomeError::Exists.
acceptance: HomeError::UnmeasuredCodexVersion { asked: "0.156.1", measured: "0.156.0" } displays a message containing both "0.156.1" and "0.156.0".
HomeError::UncarriedPart for entry id e1 and kind image displays a message containing "e1" and "image".
HomeError::BlockNotStored for entry id e1 and part index 2 displays a message containing "e1" and "2".

requirements.title: Key every account line to the block the importer stored
requirements.spec: In harness/codex/loss.rs, define the loss account and the block hash. WHEN a part on the context path is accounted, THE SYSTEM SHALL key it by the SHA-256 of serde_json::to_vec of its Claude-shaped source part, recovered by the inverse of the importer's mapping as the task lists, and SHALL take the first candidate the home's block store holds. IF no candidate is held, THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL refuse with BlockNotStored and write nothing. THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT name the SHA-256 of a re-serialised Pi part in the account. The account is one JSON object with the keys source_session, source_head, codex_version, rollout, kept, changed and lost: kept is a list of {entry, block, item}, changed a list of {entry, block, before, after, how}, lost a list of {entry, block, kind, reason}; block is null for an entry that holds no block, before and after name the source part kind and the Codex item kind, and reason is one of sidechain, harness_event, lys_entry, before_compaction, off_path, no_codex_item, opaque_thinking and empty_thinking. THE SYSTEM SHALL list every entry in the session file that is not on the context path exactly once, with block null; every part on the context path exactly once, by its entry id and block hash; and every entry on the context path that holds no block exactly once, with block null. THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT list an entry off the path, or one part, twice, and SHALL NOT carry any byte of a part's content in the account.
acceptance: For a session imported from a Claude Code file holding one text part, one tool_use part and one tool_result part, the three block hashes the account names are each found by BlockStore::get in the home the import wrote.

For a tool_result stored with its content as a single string, the account's block hash for that result equals the SHA-256 of the importer's stored bytes for it; the same holds for a tool_result stored with its content as an array and with no is_error key.
A session whose store is missing the block for one part is refused with BlockNotStored naming that entry id and part index, and the target directory holds no file afterwards.
The account's serialised object has exactly the keys changed, codex_version, kept, lost, rollout, source_head and source_session.

For the R7 second fixture session, every entry id in the session file appears in the account, each entry id off the context path appears in exactly 1 line, and each part on the context path appears in exactly 1 line, counted by its pair of entry id and block hash.

requirements.title: Map the context path to Codex 0.156.0's items, whole, with the marker last
requirements.spec: In harness/codex/rollout.rs, WHEN the context path is mapped, THE SYSTEM SHALL write, in path order: a user message's text parts as one Codex message item of role user whose content items carry each text whole; an assistant text part as a message item of role assistant carrying the text whole; a toolCall part as a function_call item with name whole, call_id equal to the tool call id, and arguments the compact JSON serialisation of the stored arguments value; a toolResult message as a function_call_output item whose call_id equals its tool call id and whose output carries the result's text whole, joining several text parts with a newline and accounting that result as changed (tool_result parts to one output); readable thinking (non-empty thinking text, not redacted) as a message item of role assistant carrying the thinking text whole, accounted as changed (before thinking, after message, how: readable thinking carried as text, signature not carried); and a compaction entry as the item kind R1 measured for it, accounted as changed. Every thinking block whose provider is not the target's (every Claude block, against an OpenAI target) is treated so, as home P3 rules. IF a thinking block is redacted, or has a signature and no readable text, THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL drop it and account it lost with reason opaque_thinking; IF it is empty and unsigned, THEN lost with reason empty_thinking. Every other part kind with no Codex item SHALL be accounted lost with reason no_codex_item. IF an image part is on the path, in a message or inside a tool result, THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL refuse with UncarriedPart naming the entry id and kind image, and write nothing. After the last mapped item, THE SYSTEM SHALL write one marker item, in the role and item kind R1 measured, whose single text is `<TRANSLATED CONTEXT from="claude-code" to="codex 0.156.0" source_session="<source session id>" source_head="<source head hash>">`, the source head hash being Session::head_hash() at render. THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT truncate, clip, summarise or note any text, argument or result, SHALL NOT carry a thinking signature or an opaque block, SHALL NOT render a sidechain entry, a custom entry or a label, and SHALL NOT use a random value or the clock for any id or timestamp.
acceptance: A session holding one user text, one assistant text, one tool call and its result maps to exactly 5 items: message (user), message (assistant), function_call, function_call_output and the marker, in that order.
A tool result of 16,384 characters maps to a function_call_output whose output has 16,384 characters and the same SHA-256 as the source text.
A tool call whose stored arguments serialise to 8,192 characters maps to a function_call whose arguments string equals serde_json::to_string of the stored arguments, 8,192 characters long.

An Anthropic thinking block with the text t1 and a signature maps to an assistant message item whose text is t1, the item carries no signature field, and the account holds one changed line for its block with before thinking and after message.
A redacted thinking block maps to no item, and the account holds one lost line naming its block hash with reason opaque_thinking.
A session whose path holds an image part is refused with UncarriedPart naming the entry id and kind image.
The last item's text equals the marker line with the fixture session's id and the session's head hash.
Mapping the same session twice gives byte-identical output.

requirements.title: Translate: check the version, refuse an existing path, write both files, record the translation beside the path
requirements.spec: In harness/codex/translate.rs, WHEN a translation is asked for a session, a target directory and a Codex version, THE SYSTEM SHALL: refuse with UnmeasuredCodexVersion when the version is not 0.156.0; compute the rollout path in the target directory under the file-name pattern R1 measured and the account path beside it as the rollout path with the extension loss.json; refuse with HomeError::Exists naming the path when either exists; map (R4) and account (R3); write the rollout and then the account, each with create_new and synced; and then append one lys.harness_event side leaf with Session::append_beside, so the head does not move, of kind codex_translation with harness codex, source_uuid null, record the hash of a manifest block naming the rollout and the account each by path and SHA-256 with the Codex version, the source session id and the source head hash, and detail {codex_version, source_head, rollout, account} holding the version, the source head hash and the two files' SHA-256, under the 512-byte cap. IF any refusal fires, THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL write no file and append no entry. THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT rewrite the session file, a block or the original Claude Code file, SHALL NOT write under the user's Codex home or any Codex thread index, and SHALL NOT run Codex (ADR-007).
acceptance: A translation asked for version 0.156.1 is refused with UnmeasuredCodexVersion naming 0.156.1 and 0.156.0, the target directory holds no file afterwards, and the session's entry count is unchanged.

With a file already at the rollout path, the translation is refused with Exists naming that path, the existing file's SHA-256 is unchanged, no account is written and the session's entry count is unchanged; the same holds with a file already at the account path.

After a translation, the session holds exactly one more entry, a lys.harness_event of kind codex_translation whose parentId is the head, the head is unchanged, and the manifest block its record names holds the rollout and account paths with SHA-256 values equal to the files' on disk.
The session file's bytes before the translation are a prefix of its bytes after it.

requirements.title: Add the render-codex subcommand with a report of paths and counts
requirements.spec: Add `render-codex` with the arguments --home, --session, --out and --codex-version, implemented in src/cli/codex.rs and dispatched from cli.rs, as cli/given.rs is. WHEN it succeeds, THE SYSTEM SHALL print one JSON report with exactly the keys rollout, account, entries, entries_rendered, blocks, kept, changed and lost: the two paths, the count of entries in the session, the count rendered, the count of blocks on the context path, and the three loss counts. IF an argument is missing, THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL exit 2 naming it. IF the translation refuses, THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL exit 1 with the refusal's message. THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT print, log or put in an error any byte of a part's content.
acceptance: render-codex on the fixture session prints a report whose keys are exactly account, blocks, changed, entries, entries_rendered, kept, lost and rollout, and whose kept, changed and lost equal the lengths of the account's three lists.
render-codex with no --codex-version exits 2 and names --codex-version.
render-codex with --codex-version 0.156.1 exits 1 and its message names 0.156.1 and 0.156.0.
cli.rs has at most 500 code lines, excluding comments and blank lines, after the change.

requirements.title: Prove the translation end to end on the fixture Claude Code file
requirements.spec: Add a fixture Claude Code file whose records carry the same user text, tool name, tool input, tool output and assistant text as the recorded fixture rollout (R1), with nothing else, and an integration test that imports it into a fresh home (HOME-001's importer), runs render-codex, and checks the card's acceptance. A second fixture session in the test adds an Anthropic signed thinking block with readable text, a redacted thinking block, a 16,384-character tool result, a sidechain, a harness event and a lys.authored entry. The test SHALL count what fired: every assertion over a list first asserts its length. THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT use fixture text as, or inside, a test name.
acceptance: The rendered rollout's response_item payloads, less the final marker item, equal the fixture rollout's response_item payloads in number and order, ignoring the fields id, call_id and turn_id, the create_time in the passthrough metadata and each line's timestamp, and comparing function_call arguments as parsed JSON.
In the rendered rollout, every function_call_output's call_id equals the call_id of exactly one function_call before it.

For the second fixture session, the account holds one changed line for the signed thinking block with before thinking and after message, one lost line for the redacted block with reason opaque_thinking, one lost line per sidechain entry with reason sidechain, one lost line for the harness event with reason harness_event and one lost line for the lys.authored entry with reason lys_entry.
For the second fixture session, the rollout carries the 16,384-character tool result whole, checked by length and SHA-256.
Rendering a second time to the same --out exits 1 naming the rollout path, and the SHA-256 of both files in the target directory is unchanged.
The Claude Code render (render_claude_code) of the fixture session to one path before render-codex and to a second path after it gives files with equal SHA-256.
A search of the report and of the account for the fixture's user text, tool output and assistant text finds 0 occurrences.

requirements.title: Write the translation into RECORD.md and the crate README
requirements.spec: Add to RECORD.md a section on the Codex translation: the loss account's keys and its kept, changed and lost lists with their fields and the eight reasons; how a block hash keys to the importer's stored block; the marker line; and the codex_translation kind of lys.harness_event with its record and detail. Add render-codex and codex_translation to the crate README. Neither document SHALL quote any transcript content.
acceptance: RECORD.md names the account keys source_session, source_head, codex_version, rollout, kept, changed and lost, the eight reasons, and the codex_translation kind with its detail keys codex_version, source_head, rollout and account.
The crate README names the render-codex subcommand and its four arguments, and the codex_translation kind.

requirements.title: Record the real resume by Codex 0.156.0 in PROOF-TRANSLATE.md
requirements.spec: Render the R7 fixture session with render-codex into the sessions tree of a fresh isolated Codex home made under a temporary directory, at the place R1 measured, then resume the thread with the Codex 0.156.0 binary by its absolute path and CODEX_HOME set to that home, and ask one question only the fixture's content answers. Write PROOF-TRANSLATE.md with: the binary's `--version` answer and which binary it was; how the isolated home was made and authenticated, with no credential; the render's report; the rollout's and the account's SHA-256 and line counts; the resume command with <codex home> in place of the directory; whether the answer held the fixture token the question asks for, as yes or no; and the SHA-256 of the Claude Code render of the same session before and after, equal. THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT put any transcript content, answer text or credential in the proof, and SHALL NOT write under the user's own Codex home.
acceptance: PROOF-TRANSLATE.md names codex-cli 0.156.0 as the `--version` answer of the binary that resumed.
PROOF-TRANSLATE.md holds the rollout's and the account's SHA-256 as 64-hex-character values, their line counts, the resume command with <codex home>, and the answer-held-token line reading yes.
PROOF-TRANSLATE.md holds two equal 64-hex-character SHA-256 values for the Claude Code render before and after.
A search of PROOF-TRANSLATE.md for the fixture's user text, tool output and assistant text finds 0 occurrences.

boundaries: No Codex to Claude Code translation, no Pi or third harness, and no launch of Codex through a launch template.
Codex's importer of Claude Code files is not adopted, vendored, linked or called, and no Codex code is copied.
No rollout shape is taken from a Codex source checkout or from a rollout another Codex version wrote; only files Codex 0.156.0 wrote are the reference.
No Codex version other than 0.156.0 is rendered for.
render.rs and the Claude Code render's output and loss account do not change by a byte.
The home session file, its blocks and the original Claude Code file are never rewritten; the translation's side leaf is an append beside the head.
Nothing is written under the user's own Codex home or into any Codex thread index, and lys-home never runs Codex.
No transcript content in the report, the account, an error, a log line, a test name or the proof; paths, ids, hashes and counts only.
No field is added to Pi's grammar; the translation record rides inside a lys.harness_event custom entry.
Image parts are refused, not carried and not dropped, until their carriage is settled.
No new code file exceeds 500 lines of code, and cli.rs stays at or under 500 code lines.
The design's structure array is the whole file list; a path outside it is not created.
verification: cargo fmt --all -- --check, cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings, cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings, cargo test --workspace --all-features, cargo doc --no-deps --all-features and cargo doc --no-deps exit 0.
